samples.text:
The line graph shows the birth rate in three countries, Country P, Country Q and Country R, between 1950 and 2020. It is measured in births per 1,000 people.

Country P had the highest birth rate for all the period. It was 44 in 1950 and it increased a little to 45 in 1960. After that it decreased steadily, it was 35 in 1980, 22 in 2000 and 15 in 2020.

Country R was the second in 1950 with 36 births. It went up to 38 in 1960 but then it fall very quickly to 20 in 1980. After 1980 it continued to decrease more slowly and in 2020 it was only 9, which was lower than Country Q.

Country Q had the lowest birth rate in most years. It started at 22 in 1950 and it goes down slowly to 14 in 1980. Then it was quite stable, about 12 or 13, and it was 11 in 2020.

Overall, the birth rates in all three countries decreased between 1950 and 2020, and Country P always was the highest.
samples.why: Basic overview at the end · key features, including the final crossover, covered · repetitive linking · tense errors, a comma splice and adverb placement errors that do not block meaning.

samples.text:
The graph illustrates changes in the birth rate, measured as the number of births per 1,000 people, in three countries labelled P, Q and R from 1950 to 2020.

Overall, birth rates fell in all three countries over the seventy years. Country P had the highest rate throughout, while Country R experienced the most dramatic decline, eventually falling below Country Q to record the lowest rate by 2020.

In 1950, there were 44 births per 1,000 people in Country P and 36 in Country R. Both figure increased slightly over the next decade, to 45 and 38 respectively. From 1960, however, the rates in both countries began to fall. Country R's rate dropped particularly sharply, almost halving to 20 between 1960 and 1980, and then continued to decline more gradually to just 9 in 2020. Country P's decrease was steadier, and its rate reached 15 at the end of the period.

Country Q, by contrast, began with a much lower birth rate of 22 in 1950. This declined gradually to 14 in 1980 and then levelled off at around 12 or 13 for three decades, before finishing at 11.
samples.why: Clear overview identifying the steepest fall and final crossover · key features logically organised · good cohesion · appropriate vocabulary · largely accurate grammar with one minor plural slip.

samples.text:
The graph compares birth rates, expressed as births per 1,000 people, in Countries P, Q and R between 1950 and 2020.

The overall trend was one of decline in all three countries, although the pace and timing varied. Country P consistently had the highest birth rate, whereas Country R, having started well above Country Q, underwent such a steep fall that it ended the period with the lowest rate.

Countries P and R initially followed a similar pattern, with their birth rates rising slightly between 1950 and 1960, to 45 and 38 respectively. Thereafter, both declined, but at very different speeds. Country R's rate plunged to 20 by 1980, and it continued to edge downwards, eventually reaching 9 in 2020, a quarter of its 1950 figure. Country P, meanwhile, experienced a more gradual but uninterrupted decrease from 1960, falling to 28 in 1990 and 15 in 2020, one third of its peak.

Country Q, by contrast, had a comparatively low birth rate from the outset, at 22 in 1950. It declined moderately to 14 by 1980 and then remained almost flat, fluctuating between 12 and 13 for three decades before dipping to 11, just above Country R's figure.
samples.why: Key features skilfully selected, including differing rates of decline · clear, well-placed overview · accurate figures and derived fractions · wide, precise vocabulary · varied, error-free structures.
